title: ISSEN vs Memrise: Features, Speaking and Best Fit
summary: October 2026 comparison of ISSEN and Memrise covering speaking practice, vocabulary tools, pricing and ideal users.
body_markdown:
Memrise built its name on spaced repetition and native-speaker video clips, and those still work for raw vocabulary. The harder question is what happens when you need to speak out loud, in real time, with someone waiting for your reply. We'll compare how Memrise's AI Buddies handle that moment versus a voice-first tutor, so you can pick the one that matches how you actually practice.


**TLDR:**


- Memrise pairs spaced repetition with native-speaker video clips across ~20+ languages, while its AI "Buddies" stay chat-based, Pro-gated, and limited to specific language pairs.
- Flashcard decks won't close the passive-to-active gap at B1 to B2; Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) explains why spoken production reps are the mechanism.
- Compare cost per rep, not sticker price: a $25 flat plan used daily runs ~$0.83 per session versus ~$3.13 twice weekly.
- Pronunciation work in ISSEN lives in a separate Shadowing mode with six regional accents (American, British, Australian, Argentinian, Mexican, Castilian), not inside live voice chats.
- ISSEN runs real-time voice conversations across 60+ languages with smart turn detection, conversation-anchored SRS, and background mode for walks or commutes.


## What is Memrise


Memrise is a vocabulary-focused language app that pairs spaced repetition with short native-speaker video clips, and more recently a set of AI chat "Buddies" (Grammar, Role Play, Translator, Culture, Conjugation, Assistant, plus MemBot) for conversational practice.


It covers roughly 20+ languages across web, iOS, and Android. Community Courses were retired from the main app in 2026, leaving the official curriculum and Pro-gated AI features as the core offering today.


## What is ISSEN


ISSEN is a[real-time AI voice tutor](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-voice-tutors-language-learning/) covering 60+ languages across iOS, Android, and web. Sessions start in under 30 seconds with no push-to-talk, and the tutor drives the conversation, adapts to your level, and remembers context between sessions. Vocabulary review is anchored to sentences you actually spoke, and pronunciation drills live in a separate Shadowing mode. ISSEN works best as one input inside a broader study plan that still includes grammar instruction and reading.


## Speaking practice and conversation depth


Memrise's speaking practice runs through AI Buddies (Grammar, Role Play, Translator, Culture, Conjugation, Assistant) plus the earlier MemBot. These are chat-based tutors gated to Pro, with free users getting a capped taste,[per Nabu's breakdown](https://www.hellonabu.com/blog/en/is-memrise-free/) . Rollout is limited to specific language pairs, per[Memrise's help docs](https://memrisebeta.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/29222065964817-Introducing-AI-buddies) .


ISSEN runs[real-time voice conversations](https://www.issen.com/blog/how-ai-speaking-practice-works/) with smart turn detection, so there is no push-to-talk. The tutor opens the session, picks a topic, and adjusts pace to your level. Background and lock-screen mode lets you keep talking while walking or commuting.


## Vocabulary, SRS and memory features


Memrise's SRS is one of its oldest strengths: large decks across 20+ languages, each word paired with short native-speaker video clips that train the ear in a way synthetic audio cannot.[Reviewers note](https://www.alllanguageresources.com/memrise-review-good-beginners-dont-overuse/) it works well for raw memorization.


ISSEN generates[flashcards from spaced repetition](https://www.issen.com/blog/spaced-repetition-vocabulary-ai-conversation-practice/) tied to sentences you actually spoke, so each card carries the grammatical context from your own utterance. Cross-session memory then resurfaces missed forms inside later conversations.


If you want curated decks with authentic native-speaker clips, Memrise is the stronger fit, while ISSEN is the better choice when you want retention tied to the sentences you actually produced in conversation.


## Pronunciation and accent support


Memrise's pronunciation exposure runs through native-speaker video clips, which give you authentic models to copy but no structured feedback. Pro users in supported pairs get limited pronunciation practice through AI tools, though coverage varies.


ISSEN splits this work into two places.[Shadowing](https://www.issen.com/blog/shadowing-pronunciation-technique/) is a separate mode with pause-and-repeat drills across six regional accents: American, British, Australian, Argentinian, Mexican, and Castilian. For conversation, you can pick an accent-specific tutor. One caveat: ISSEN does not give pronunciation feedback inside voice conversations. Shadowing is where that work happens.


## Language coverage and content depth


Memrise officially supports roughly 20+ languages, including Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, and Yoruba. User-generated Community Courses were retired from the main app in 2026, so what remains is officially curated.


ISSEN covers 60+ languages for voice tutoring, including less commonly taught ones that rarely get[real speaking tools](https://www.issen.com/blog/rosetta-stone-alternatives-ai-voice-tutor/) built around them.


If you want polished official content in a narrower set, Memrise fits. If your target language sits outside the big twenty and you still want voice practice, ISSEN is the broader bet.


## Pricing and free trial


Memrise offers a free tier with core lessons, basic SRS, native-speaker video clips, and a capped sample of AI conversation. Unlimited speaking and most AI Buddy features sit behind Pro,[per Nabu's breakdown](https://www.hellonabu.com/blog/en/is-memrise-free/) . Check current Pro pricing on memrise.com before subscribing.


ISSEN, one of the[Speak app alternatives](https://www.issen.com/blog/speak-app-alternatives/) worth comparing, runs $20 to $29 USD per month, flat rate, unlimited daily practice, with a 10-minute free trial.

## Who each app suits best


### Memrise fits you if


- You want curated vocabulary decks with native-speaker video clips
- You enjoy gamified memorization and streak-driven word study
- You want occasional chatbot role-play as a supplement, not the core


### ISSEN fits you if


You are past the beginner stage (B1 or above), can read your target language, but freeze when someone asks you a question out loud. The audience is concrete: immigrants handling work and daily life in a second language, remote workers on English-language calls, healthcare professionals switching registers with patients, and busy parents with 10-minute gaps between meetings, the same crowd that browses[Speak competitors and alternatives](https://www.issen.com/blog/speak-competitors-alternatives/) . If your constraint is voice reps that fit a real schedule, ISSEN is the closer match.

## Memrise strengths and limitations


### What it does well


- Strong SRS engine with native-speaker video clips tied to real pronunciation
- Polished mobile UX and a usable free tier for vocabulary review
- Broad library of curated content across 20+ languages


### Where it falls short


- AI Buddies are chat-based, not real-time voice, and gated to Pro
- Buddy rollout covers a limited set of language pairs
- Community Courses retirement in 2026 narrowed user-generated depth
- Speaking production under conversational pressure stays underbuilt


Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) is the frame: recognition does not automatically convert into spoken production. A vocabulary-first app can grow your passive store indefinitely and leave the passive-to-active gap intact, the same pattern[Copycat Cafe flags in its Memrise review](https://copycatcafe.com/blog/memrise) .


## ISSEN strengths and limitations


### What it does well


- Real-time voice conversation with smart turn detection, no push-to-talk
- 60+ languages, including ones that rarely get voice tools built around them
- Conversation-anchored SRS: flashcards pulled from sentences you actually spoke
- Dedicated Shadowing mode with six regional accents (American, British, Australian, Argentinian, Mexican, Castilian)
- Background and lock-screen mode converts walks and commutes into reps
- Flat monthly pricing with unlimited daily practice


### Where it falls short


- No pronunciation feedback inside live voice conversations; that work lives in Shadowing
- Not built for complete beginners who want a structured, step-by-step lesson path
- Does not replace a human tutor for cultural pragmatics or fossilized-error correction


The straight framing: ISSEN is the daily speaking layer. A weekly Preply or italki session still earns its place for correction depth. The two stack well, and if you're weighing chat-based options too, our[ISSEN vs Talkpal comparison](https://www.issen.com/blog/issen-talkpal-comparison/) covers that ground.


## Best Overall AI Voice Tutor: ISSEN


Memrise earns its place as a vocabulary companion. The decks are solid, the native-speaker clips are useful, and AI Buddies give you a chat-based taste of practice. What it does not give you is real-time voice conversation at the volume intermediate learners need to close the passive-active gap, a gap we also unpack in[ISSEN vs Duolingo for speaking practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-app-speaking-issen-duolingo/) .


That is where ISSEN sits. Voice-first, 60+ languages, smart turn detection, conversation-anchored SRS, and a separate Shadowing mode for pronunciation work, the kind of design covered in our look at[how AI language learning platforms work](https://www.issen.com/blog/ai-vs-standard-language-learning-apps/) .


Start a 10-minute conversation with an ISSEN tutor today, then come back tomorrow. The reps compound.


## Final thoughts on the best Memrise alternative for speaking


Memrise does the vocabulary layer well, so keep it if that is the gap you are filling. For the passive-to-active jump, you need voice conversations stacked across weeks, not more flashcards. The reps that matter are the ones you take tomorrow, the day after, and the week after that, because conversational fluency is a cumulative skill that only compounds when speaking practice becomes part of your daily cadence rather than something you schedule once and hope will stick. Pick the cadence you can actually sustain, pair it with the vocabulary and grammar work you are already doing, and treat each session as one more rep toward the moment someone asks you a question out loud and the answer arrives without a translation step in the middle.[Start a 10-minute conversation with ISSEN](https://www.issen.com/) and let the reps compound from there.


## FAQ


### Should I pick ISSEN or Memrise if I only have 10 minutes a day to practice?


If those 10 minutes are the only speaking reps you'll get, ISSEN is the better fit. The tutor opens the session, drives it, and runs in background mode while you walk or commute. Memrise's 10 minutes will go further on vocabulary retention through its SRS and native-speaker clips, but spoken production stays underbuilt.


### Can I use Memrise and ISSEN together instead of choosing one?


Yes, and for many intermediate learners that's the realistic answer. Memrise handles vocabulary intake and listening exposure through curated decks; ISSEN handles the daily speaking reps and anchors review flashcards to sentences you actually produced. They cover different sides of the passive-to-active gap.


### Is ISSEN worth it if I'm a complete beginner in a new language?


Probably not as your primary tool. ISSEN is built for learners around B1 and above who can already read the target language but freeze when speaking. Beginners usually get more traction starting with a structured curriculum (Memrise's decks, a textbook, or a scenario-based app) and layering ISSEN in once they have a vocabulary base to produce from.


### Does ISSEN correct my pronunciation during conversations like Memrise's native-speaker clips train it?


No, and this is worth being clear about. ISSEN does not give pronunciation feedback inside live voice conversations. That work lives in the separate Shadowing mode, which has pause-and-repeat drills across six regional accents. Memrise's video clips give you authentic models to copy but no structured feedback either; neither tool replaces targeted phonetic coaching.


### How does ISSEN's pricing actually compare to Memrise Pro once I'm practicing daily?


Memrise's sticker price is lower, but cost-per-rep is the number that matters. See the cost-per-session breakdown in the pricing table above and run the same arithmetic against Memrise Pro's current rate and your realistic weekly cadence; remember that the AI Buddy conversation on Memrise Pro is capped and limited to specific language pairs. Check memrise.com for current Pro pricing before you commit.
